The patient presents with acute, non-traumatic left wrist pain of 3-day duration, now worsening. Key red flags include leukocytosis (WBC 15,000/μL) — a nonspecific but important marker of systemic inflammatory or infectious activity — in the absence of local signs (no swelling, erythema, warmth, or bruising). The absence of trauma and localized inflammatory signs makes *overt* cellulitis or septic arthritis less immediately apparent, yet the elevated WBC strongly argues against purely mechanical or degenerative causes (e.g., tendinopathy) or chronic autoimmune flares without acute inflammation (e.g., stable RA).  

Among the differential, *septic arthritis* remains the most time-sensitive and dangerous diagnosis: it can present with minimal or even absent local signs early on (“occult septic arthritis”), especially in immunocompetent adults, and leukocytosis is common (though not universal). Crystal arthropathies (gout/pseudogout) typically cause prominent local inflammation (swelling, warmth, exquisite tenderness) — all explicitly *denied* here. Early RA rarely presents with isolated acute wrist pain and marked leukocytosis without other systemic or joint findings (e.g., morning stiffness, symmetric involvement, RF/ACPA positivity — none reported). Osteomyelitis would usually require antecedent trauma, puncture, or risk factors (e.g., diabetes, IV drug use), none of which are present.  

The provisional impression correctly prioritizes infection and inflammation, but the *combination* of acute monoarticular wrist pain + unexplained leukocytosis + absence of alternative explanatory signs points most urgently to *septic arthritis* — particularly because it mandates immediate intervention (e.g., aspiration, antibiotics) if confirmed. Pending imaging (X-ray, ultrasound/Doppler) and labs (CRP/ESR, uric acid) are appropriate, but the clinical weight of leukocytosis in this context tips the balance toward infection as the leading concern — not as a certainty, but as the single most likely and highest-consequence diagnosis requiring urgent exclusion.

- Provisional impression includes septic arthritis as a top consideration, aligned with clinical urgency

Septic arthritis
